sections.title: The Liege Meeting
sections.content: The Association of Electrical Engineers of the Montefiore Institute organized an international meeting on minicomputers and data communication in Liege, Belgium. The meeting was scheduled for January 20–22, 1975, at the Palais des Congres.
sections.plainLanguage: The organizers planned a meeting in Liege about minicomputers and data communication. It was scheduled for January 20–22, 1975.

sections.title: Topics and Paper Submissions
sections.content:
The call invites papers on minicomputer architecture, protocol definition and representation, software organization, fault-tolerant computing, system evaluation and simulation, terminal pooling, computer networks and packet switching.

Authors were asked to submit a title and 500-word summary by June 1, 1974, with their company affiliation and a short biography. Accepted authors would be notified before July 1 and asked to submit full manuscripts before September 1, 1974.
sections.plainLanguage: Authors could submit work on computer design, protocols, software, reliability, networks and related topics. They were asked for a title, summary and biographical information by the stated deadline.

sections.title: Presentations and Languages
sections.content: Each presentation was limited to 30 minutes to leave time for discussion. Papers and presentations could be in English or French, and simultaneous translation would be available. The announcement directs submissions to Professor A. Danthine at the University of Liege.
sections.plainLanguage: Presentations could be in English or French, with simultaneous translation. Each talk had a 30-minute limit.
